findings.title: Faded pillars leave their cap, plinth, rail and switch plaque floating in mid-air
findings.problem: When a hazard pillar comes between the camera and Pip, only the 1.4×3×1.4 m body fades. The body is on game.root and registered in game.occluders. The orange cap slab (y 3.02), the BASE plinth (y 0.08), the rail band (y 1.06) and the small cream plaque (y 0.35) are on decorRoot, which freeze() merges into opaque meshes, so they never fade. At the close camera (zoom 9) the player sees an opaque orange tabletop floating in the air above Pip, a brown tray on the floor and a cream square hovering at knee height, with a ghostly hazard texture in between. This happens whenever Pip passes behind pillar-a (-1.3,-1.3) or pillar-b (3.2,2.7), and both sit on the clean route and the slingshot run. It reads as broken geometry exactly when the camera is meant to be helping. It also breaks the occlusion rule: the cap still hides part of the view, and a stray outline ghost shows around the faded body.
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:53-62 (pillar(): body on game.root + occluders; base/cap/rail/plaque on r=game.decorRoot)
findings.fix: In decor.ts pillar(): build the plinth, cap, rail and plaque as children of one group on game.root, each with a cloned transparent material (material.clone(); transparent=true), and push each mesh into game.occluders. Simpler alternative: parent them under the faded body mesh `m` and in game.ts:388 traverse occluder children so the whole assembly shares one opacity. Fade the plaque too, or drop it. Use the same fade target (≤0.25) and keep depthWrite on so sorting stays stable (DR-78). Better still, switch occluder fades to alpha-hash/dither (material.alphaHash=true) so outlines do not ghost.
findings.verify: Re-run mockups/review5/tools/playground-models/b.mjs (visit pillar-a at zoom 9) and retake playground-models-18 and -20. No orange slab should hover above Pip, and the base and cap should fade together with the body.
findings.verify_reason: Checked in code and reproduced. decor.ts:55 puts only the pillar body on game.root with a transparent clone and pushes it into occluders. decor.ts:56/59 put the plinth, the orange cap slab, the rail band and the cream plaque on decorRoot, which freeze() merges, and game.ts:387-388 fades only this.occluders. My own zoom-9 shot behind pillar-a shows exactly what the finding describes: an opaque orange cap floating above Pip, a brown plinth tray on the floor, an orange rail band and a cream square in mid-air, with a ghost hazard texture in between.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-04-behind-pillar-a-close.jpg (Pip at -1.3,-2.6, zoom 9: floating cap, rail, plinth and plaque)
src/game.ts:388 sets opacity only on meshes in this.occluders
findings.fix_correction: The fix is right, with one caution. toon() returns shared cached materials (toon(BASE), toon(CAP), toon(RAIL) are reused by the shell walls and interior walls), so each pillar part must get its own material.clone() before transparent=true. Otherwise every wall rail and cap in the room fades together.

findings.title: The lamp has no switch: 'Switch the lamp on' targets the bare base of the post
findings.problem: Step 3 of the tutorial is 'Switch the lamp on', and the room is supposed to teach that a switch closes the loop. But there is no switch model anywhere. level.switchAt is (7.55,-6.35), which is exactly the centre of the lamp post (decor.ts:89 places the lamp group at target+(0.55,-0.35)). The player presses E anywhere within 1.9 m of the post and the lamp lights. Nothing in the world flips, clicks over or changes state apart from the bulb. The objective marker for this step is drawn at the same point, so the post skewers the bouncing cone. The only rule this room teaches about electricity, 'the circuit is open until the switch closes it', is never shown by an object, and players get no idea what a switch looks like before the Meeting projector switch. It also leaves 'plugged in but off' invisible: before E the lamp looks exactly like the unpowered lamp.
evidence: src/game.ts:217 and :244 (E toggles switchedOn within 1.9 m; no mesh is updated)
src/ui/objectives.ts:26 (marker at switchAt), :118 (marker at fixed y 2.1)
mockups/review5/shots/playground-models-45-plugged-close.jpg (marker cone pierced by the post; nothing to switch)
findings.fix: In decor.ts playground() add a wall-box switch on the camera-facing side of the post at y 1.1: a housing rbox(.18,.26,.09,.03) in '#f0ece2' at (t.x+.55, 1.1, t.z-.35+.12), an INK rocker or toggle box(.05,.11,.05) pivoting about x, and a pilot dot sphere(.025) in INK (off) or lit('#57e38f') (on). Return the toggle and pilot meshes through Decor (for example decor.switch). Add a short conduit tube from the socket up the post to the switch so the loop is visible: socket → switch → bulb. In game.ts:217, rotate the toggle to ±0.45 rad and swap the pilot material when switchedOn changes. Move level.switchAt to the switch's front (7.55,-6.0) so the marker sits over the switch rather than the post. Optional: when connected but off, give the bulb a faint 'ready' tint so 'powered but open' reads.
findings.verify: Take a zoom-9 shot at (6.6,-5.9) before and after E (script d.mjs, shots -45/-46). The toggle visibly changes position and the pilot dot changes colour. A first-time viewer can point at 'the switch' without the HUD. The marker no longer intersects the post.
findings.verify_reason: playground.ts:6 sets switchAt=(7.55,-6.35). decor.ts:89 places the lamp group at target+(.55,-.35), which is the same point. The lamp is built from a base, post, arm, shade and bulb only; no switch geometry exists. game.ts:217 only flips switchedOn, plays a sound and fires sparks. objectives.ts:118 draws the marker at y 2.1 on the post's axis. My plugged-in close-up shows the yellow marker cone skewered by the post, and nothing in the scene reads as a switch.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-16-plugged-close.jpg (marker cone pierced by the post; no switch)

findings.title: The lamp's socket is a blank dark box, built twice, and the plug's pins come out of its back
findings.problem: The socket the whole job aims at is a featureless #384454 cube. It has no face plate, no slots and no pilot light, so it reads as a brick or a speaker, not a socket. That clashes with the practice-wall sockets (cream plates with holes) and with the how-to poster. It is also built twice in the same spot. game.ts:88 adds a plain unrounded BoxGeometry(.48,.38,.3) at y 0.25, and decor.ts:92 adds an rbox(.48,.38,.3) at y 0.20. Their side faces are coplanar, a z-fighting risk that is masked only because the colours are identical, and the box gets no outline from the kit's rounded edges. When the plug connects, the plug mesh is pushed into the box: its gold pins poke out of the back face (crop -58). The teal target torus (r .42, tube .07, at y .15) runs into the lamp's black base disc (r .42 at 0.65 m away), so the two flat discs interpenetrate at floor level.
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:89 (lamp base cyl r .34/.42 at y .08, centre 0.65 m from the socket)
findings.verify: Retake playground-models-45 and -58 with d.mjs. The socket shows a plate and slots at the game camera, the plug head sits flush in the plate, no gold pins show on the far side, and the ring no longer cuts the lamp base. A two-frame diff at zoom 9 while orbiting shows no flicker on the socket sides.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:88 adds a plain BoxGeometry(.48,.38,.3) at y .25, and decor.ts:92 adds an rbox(.48,.38,.3) at y .20 at the same x/z. That is a duplicate with coplanar sides. My devtools probe found the BoxGeometry and the torus at (7,-6); the rbox is merged into decorRoot. In my win push-in, two gold pins stick out of the far face of the dark box. The socket is a featureless dark cube at every angle I captured, and the cyan torus overlaps the black lamp base disc.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-20-win-pushin.jpg (gold pins poking out of the socket's back face)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-16-plugged-close.jpg and -17-plugged-close-o450.png (blank dark box; ring meets base disc)
probe: meshes at target = TorusGeometry y .15 + BoxGeometry y .25

findings.title: The cable runs through Pip's body, head and feet (P3 still open)
findings.problem:
The cable's last segment goes from the rope's end (Pip's centre) straight to the right glove, so it nearly always passes through Pip:
- Idle carry (shot -41): the hose comes from the reel, enters Pip's lower back and the plug pops out of the glove on the other side.
- Near the strain limit (shot -44, crop -60): the pull pose raises the hand beside the hard hat, so the 20 cm-thick orange cable climbs through the shoulder and the hat brim, and the plug is hidden behind the head.
- Plugged in and at the win push-in (shots -45, -46, -47): the gold cable lies straight through Pip's boots.
This is the R2 'cable through the legs' bug and is still unfixed. The cable is the star of the game and Pip is the hero, so the two most-watched objects visibly clip in the tutorial's hero shots.
findings.fix: In game.ts drawCable(), after cablePath, re-route the tail around Pip's capsule. Find the last path point within 0.5 m of Pip's axis. Replace the inside points with a waypoint at Pip pos + (heading-right × 0.42) at y 0.55 (a 'belt loop' on the hand side), then go to the hand. While connected and Pip stands within 0.6 m of the cable, push the rope's floor points out of the 0.36 m capsule radius before building the hose. Cap the pull-pose hand height (pipRig) at y 1.2 so the plug never rises past the chest, which also satisfies DR-65.
findings.verify: Add a check script that, for every frame of d.mjs, measures the minimum distance from the hose's centre-line points to Pip's capsule segment (radius 0.32). Expect ≥ 0.32 + hose radius except within 0.15 m of the glove. Retake -41, -44, -45 and -47.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:293-294 draws the cable from the rope end to the glove with cablePath and does nothing to avoid Pip's body. My hold-plug side view shows the white hose going from the reel into Pip's lower back. My plugged-in close-up shows the gold cable passing straight through Pip's boots.

findings.title: Coworkers have no colliders: Pip walks into the trainees and their bodies clip through Pip
findings.problem: addNpc() builds only a visual group. No Rapier body or collider is created, so Pip's character controller, thrown props and the cable all pass through the three trainees. Walking to the supply cage put Pip's centre 0.41 m from the teal trainee at (-6.6,-3.4). The blob's body visibly intersects Pip's arm and legs (shots -13 and -14), and the mug-holding arm sticks through Pip's torso. Thrown boxes fly through blobs instead of bonking them. That costs the 'world reacts to chaos' comedy and looks like a clipping bug in the first room a player sees. g.audit() cannot catch it because it only tests coworkers against fixed colliders and props at load.
findings.fix: In addNpc(), for standing NPCs, create a fixed rigid body at (p.x,.55,p.z) with ColliderDesc.capsule(.22,.33) (matching the blob capsule .33 radius and .35 length) and friction .5. For seated ones use a ball(.33) at the seat height. Store the collider on the Npc so the alarm() logic can also fire when a prop contacts it (a bonk reaction). The audit at game.ts:498 keeps working, since it then sees them as fixed colliders.
findings.verify: Script: walkTo(-6.6,-3.4) from (-7,-1). The final distance from Pip to the trainee stays ≥ 0.66 m. Retake playground-models-13 and -14: no interpenetration. Throw a box (Space) at a trainee: it bounces off and snap().alarmed ≥ 1.
findings.verify_reason: addNpc (game.ts:127-134) builds only a T.Group; no rigid body or collider is created, and NPCs never move except for visual squash. I reproduced it: walkTo(-6.6,-3.4) ended with Pip 0.10 m from the teal trainee's centre, and the screenshot shows the two bodies fully interpenetrating, with the trainee's face and mug sticking out of Pip's torso.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-03-trainee-overlap-close.jpg (Pip and teal trainee merged; distance 0.10 m)
findings.fix_correction: The fix needs one more change. audit() (game.ts:497-498) tests each standing coworker's Ball(.36) against every fixed collider. Once NPCs get fixed colliders, each coworker will report an overlap with its own collider. Store the collider handle on the Npc and skip it in the audit, or tag NPC colliders and exclude them from the fixed list. A fixed body is fine, because NPCs never translate.

findings.title: Beanbags still read as bread loaves or burger buns, in cardboard brown
findings.problem: There are six beanbags, from three 'lounge' clusters: (-9.09,-1.67), (-7.99,-1.52), (-1.33,1.73), (-0.23,1.88), (1.02,6.67), (0.87,7.77). Each is a flattened sphere plus a second squashed sphere with a thin torus seam. The lounge recipe picks their colour from the default FLOOR kraft palette (#c98f5a/#d7a56d/#e0b47a), so they are the same brown as the cardboard boxes. At the game camera they read as bread rolls, brioche or potatoes (start, survey). At zoom 9 the two even lobes read as a burger bun or a cinnamon bun (shots -14, -15, -19). There is no seat dent you can read, no pinched top and no fabric colour. They also share the box colour family, which breaks DR-51 (fabric is saturated, cardboard is kraft). R2, F5 and P5 flagged this; it is not fixed. The g.audit(.02) overlaps found at start are also all beanbag-related: paper sheets tucked 3 cm inside three beanbags.
evidence: src/props/prefabs.ts:130-136 (beanbag: two spheres + torus + dark disc)
src/levels/clutter.ts:38 (lounge picks color from c) and :53 (FLOOR browns), src/levels/playground.ts:5 (no colors passed)
findings.fix:
Model (prefabs.ts beanbag case):
- Replace the two spheres with one LatheGeometry pear profile: radius 0.44 at the base, 0.30 at 0.42 m, a pinched top of 0.12 at 0.58 m. Tilt it back 0.18 rad.
- Carve a seat dent: a darker sphere(.22) scaled (1,.25,1) and sunk at the front, at z +.12, y bottom+.36.
- Add 3 vertical seam tubes (Tube r .012) from the base to the pinched top, and a small carry tab box(.12,.05,.03) at the top.
- Use 24+ segments.
Colour:
- Give recipes per-kind palettes. In clutter.ts, pass a FABRIC list for beanbag and chair, CHAIRC filtered to ΔE>15 from every BLOBC hue, for example '#e5484d', '#3f7fd6', '#6cc58a'.
- Keep FLOOR only for box.
Layout: shift the lounge 'paper' item to dz .9 so it doesn't spawn inside the beanbag.
findings.verify: Retake playground-models-01, -15 and -19, and a silhouette sheet with tools/debug/gallery.mjs at 26 m and 10 m. A viewer says 'beanbag' unprompted. g.audit(.02) reports zero overlaps at playground start.
findings.verify_reason: prefabs.ts:130-136 builds the beanbag from two squashed spheres, a torus and a dark disc. clutter.ts:38 picks the colour from c, which defaults to FLOOR browns (clutter.ts:53, 61) because playground.ts passes no colors. g.audit(.02) reproduced exactly the three beanbag×paper overlaps of 0.03 m. My close-up near the cage shows two kraft-brown lumps that read as bread loaves.
extra_evidence: v1.mjs audit02 output: the same three beanbag/paper overlaps at 0.03
findings.fix_correction: Lower the priority to P2. The beanbags break DR-51 and DR-52 and look wrong, but they don't hurt teaching or play. In the fix, also give beanbags a round collider (ball or capsule, per DR-71) to replace the 0.9×0.6×0.9 cuboid.

findings.title: The bowling pins fall when Pip just walks into them, so the slingshot bonus comes free; they also read as white cones
findings.problem:
The pins exist to give the slingshot a reward (R4B, P4). But they are ordinary 'cone' props (mass 1, a 0.5×0.62×0.5 box collider), and Pip's character controller pushes dynamic bodies (setApplyImpulsesToDynamicBodies). Walking to (3.6,4.6) bowled all six. The confetti burst fired and the 'Knock down all six pins' star lit at 0:19 without the cable ever being touched (shot -33: three stars, confetti, pins scattered). The signature chaos toy is short-circuited by walking.
Visually, each pin is a traffic cone with a square base plate, recoloured #fffaf0. Its stripe band (#fff6e6) disappears on white, so the six read as white cones, meringues or soft-serve swirls (shot -30), not bowling pins. They also sit only about 20 luma above the 205-luma floor (pins 225), against the ≥25 target. With their square bases the six pins tile into a grid.
evidence: src/game.ts:82 (setApplyImpulsesToDynamicBodies(true)), :251-253 (pinsDown: tipped or slid 0.5 m), :347 (strike confetti)
findings.fix:
1. Add a 'pin' PropKind in prefabs.ts.
   - Model: a LatheGeometry bowling-pin profile 0.7 m tall (base r .09, belly r .12 at .22 m, neck r .05 at .48 m, head r .07 at .62 m), white #fffaf0.
   - Detail: two red #e5484d neck stripes (torus or cylinder bands at .44 and .50 m).
   - No base plate; 24+ segments.
   - Collider: cylinder or capsule, mass 1.5.
   - Use it in playground.ts:17.
2. Count a strike only when the pins were hit by the cable or a flung prop. In slingshot() (game.ts:257), tag props within 1.1 m of the rope as flung for 2 s. In pinsDown(), only count a pin if the last contact came from a flung prop or the rope, or if Pip was not within 0.8 m when it tipped. Alternatively, raise pin mass so that Pip's walking push (65 kg controller impulse) only wobbles them, and let tipping need a hit faster than 3 m/s.
3. Paint a bowling-lane decal (two gutter lines and an arrow) from the crate row toward the pins, so the target reads in the survey.
findings.verify: Script: walk straight through the pins and advance 2 s. snap().pinsDown is 0, and the bonus star stays unlit. Run the routes.spec 'slingshot' sequence aimed at the pins: pinsDown reaches 6 and confetti fires. Retake playground-models-30: a viewer names 'bowling pins'.
findings.verify_reason: The pins are kind 'cone' (playground.ts:18), with mass 1 and a cuboid collider. The controller pushes dynamic bodies (game.ts:83), and pinsDown also counts a pin slid 0.5 m (game.ts:252-253). I reproduced it: walking eight short passes through the triangle without touching the plug knocked all 6 down. The bonus stars lit (3/3 at 0:09) and confetti fired. A single walk-through knocked down 3. The prompt over them reads 'Grab the cone', and they render as white traffic cones.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-10-walk-only-strike.jpg (pinsDown 6, stars 3/3, confetti, holdingPlug false, rope length 0.99)
mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-06-walked-through-pins.jpg (3 down after one walk-through; prompt 'Grab the cone')
findings.fix_correction: Pins can also be picked up with E and carried 0.5 m, which counts as 'down' (game.ts:253). Make pins non-grabbable: exclude spec.id 'pin-*' in nearest(), or only count a tip and not a slide. Otherwise the bonus can still be farmed by carrying them.

findings.title: The job item (the plug) starts hidden under Pip's feet, so the first frame shows no goal
findings.problem: plugPosition = anchor + (0.7, 0.3, 0.7) = (-7.3,0.3,4.7). Spawn is (-7,5), only 0.42 m away. Pip's capsule (r .32) and body cover the plug completely from the default camera (yaw 0.14, looking −z). In the start shot the reel is visible, but the 'reel's plug' named on the card cannot be seen. The bouncing objective marker hangs above Pip's head, over the beanbags behind, and at zoom 9 its cone drops into Pip's hard hat (shot -62). The grab-cue brackets frame Pip's boots rather than an object (shot -11). The first-ever instruction in the game ('Pick up the reel's plug') points at something the player cannot see. The three highest-contrast shapes (Pip, held item, goal) collapse into one.
findings.fix: Move the plug's rest spot to the camera side of the reel and clear of spawn. In game.ts:85, use anchor + (0.15, 0.15, 0.95), which gives (-7.85,.15,4.95), and lay it on its side facing +x. Move spawn to (-6.0,5.4) in playground.ts:6, and shift the START tape (decor.ts:105-107 follows l.spawn). That leaves about 1.9 m between Pip and the plug, with the plug in plain view in front of the yellow reel. In objectives.ts:118, set the marker height to max(2.1, Pip head + 0.6) when the target is within 1 m of Pip, so it never sits in the hat.
findings.verify: Retake playground-models-01 (a.mjs). The yellow plug is visible as a distinct object in the start frame, and the marker hovers over it with no overlap with Pip. Check routes.spec 'playground cable physically reaches…' still passes, since F picks up within reach.
findings.verify_reason: The plug rests at anchor+(.7,.3,.7)=(-7.3,.3,4.7), 0.42 m from spawn (-7,5) and on the far side of Pip from the default camera. In my start shot and its enlarged crop, the plug is not readable as an object. Only the reel, a small white hose stub and the yellow reticle bracket show beside Pip's elbow, and the marker cone hangs above Pip's head. In the reviewer's shot -62 the dropped plug's marker sits in the hat. The claim that it is 'completely' hidden is slightly overstated, because the reticle and hose stub do show.
findings.fix_correction: Lower the priority to P2. The 'F Pick up the plug' prompt pill shows at once, and F works from spawn, so play is not blocked or misled. If spawn moves, also check the clutter spawn keep-out (clutter.ts:78) and the lane start points in playground.ts:6, which use [-7,5]. Update them to the new spawn so the clutter layout doesn't shift unexpectedly.

findings.title: False job items: dead practice sockets with a green 'live' light, a spare reel and a job-yellow splitter
findings.problem:
Three things in the tutorial look like parts of the job but do nothing:
1. The 'practice wall' is five socket plates on the back wall at x -6…-1.2, y .55, all in easy reach (the plug reaches with 14 m of the 19 m reel). One of them glows green, the universal 'live here' cue. Dragging the plug there and pressing F just drops it (shot -62: holdingPlug false, connected undefined). There is no click, no buzz and no 'wrong socket' cue. A new player can reasonably think the green socket is the goal and that the game is broken.
2. The 'parts' clutter recipe spawns a second, grabbable cable reel (brown flanges) at (-4.51,-8.93) and a splitter at (-3.81,-8.53) right under that wall. The splitter keeps its job-yellow #ffc94d default, and the prompt reads 'Grab the splitter' (shot -17).
3. The supply cage holds a job-yellow reel and a red reel that look exactly like the anchor reel.
In the first level, where the player learns what a job item looks like, the room teaches them that yellow reels, splitters and green-lit sockets are noise.
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:96-99 (practice wall, green glow at k===2)
src/levels/clutter.ts:45 (parts recipe: reel + splitter), src/levels/playground.ts:5 ('parts' in recipes)
findings.fix:
Practice wall: make it work as a warm-up. Add practice sockets as extra snap targets in game.ts (the same forgiving rule as :204-205). Plugging in lights a small LED beside the socket with a click and a happy chirp, without completing the job, so plugging is learned by doing. Otherwise remove the green glow and blank the plates off with X-taped covers.
Clutter: drop 'parts' from the playground recipes in playground.ts:5, or recolour the parts recipe in clutter.ts:45 (reel flanges '#9aa3b2', splitter '#c7ccd6'). Make every non-job prop avoid ΔE<25 of #ffc94d/#ffc629.
Cage: recolour the cage reels to DMETAL/'#c7ccd6'.
findings.verify: Retake playground-models-17, -21 and -61. Count the props within 25 ΔE of job yellow in the start and survey shots: only the anchor reel, the plug and the lamp shade remain. Then test the practice wall: either it lights an LED on F, or it carries no live cue.
findings.verify_reason: decor.ts:97 adds a green glow at practice socket k===2. clutter.ts:45 places a reel and a splitter, and the splitter gets no colour, so it keeps the default #ffc94d (prefabs.ts:24). The cage reels are #ffc94d/#e5484d (decor.ts:112). I reproduced the practice wall: holding the plug at (-3.6,-8.7) with strain .72 and pressing F just drops it (holding false, electrical off), with no feedback. The green 'live' socket is visible on the back wall in my pillar shot.

findings.title: Bookshelves and the supply cage don't fade, so they hide Pip on the clean route
findings.problem: Only pillars and interior walls are occluders. The room's five 1.8 m bookshelves are dynamic props drawn as InstancedMesh batches, so they cannot fade. The 1.8 m supply cage is frozen decor. The bookshelf at (-3.64,-6.52), rotated along z, stands between the camera and the clean route's second leg toward (-4,-4) and the practice wall. At the close camera it covers Pip completely except for the hard hat (shots -17, -21). The bookshelves at (1.95,-1.4) and (4.47,1.07) do the same next to the pillars in the survey and orbit views. DR-12 sets 1.2 m as the fade threshold and names shelves and racks.
evidence: src/game.ts:139-142 (batchProps: props become InstancedMesh, not occluders)
src/game.ts:387-388 (single ray to p.y+.4, only this.occluders)
findings.fix: In game.ts batchProps(), keep props taller than 1.2 m (bookshelf, cabinet, vending, cooler, plant ≥1.25) out of the batch. Leave them as individual meshes with cloned transparent materials and push their meshes into this.occluders. There are 5 to 7 in this room, so the draw-call cost is small. Raycast to three points (feet y .2, chest .9, head 1.6) instead of one (game.ts:387). Move the cage to game.root with transparent materials registered as occluders.
findings.verify: Sweep 8 yaws at zoom 9 and 38 with Pip at (-4,-7) and (2,-2). At least 70% of Pip's pixels stay visible (mask by Pip's colours). Retake playground-models-17 and -21.
findings.verify_reason: In code, batchProps (game.ts:139-142) turns every prop into InstancedMesh, so none can fade, and the cage is frozen decor. The reviewer's shot -17 shows a bookshelf covering all of Pip but the hat at the practice wall. However, the claim that this happens 'on the clean route' is not supported. From the default camera (+z, looking −z), the shelves at z -6.52, -1.4 and 1.07 sit behind or below the ray to Pip on the lane (-4,-4)→(5.8,-5.5). By my geometry the ray clears 1.8 m at both zoom 17 and zoom 9. Pip is hidden only near the practice wall (off-route) or at orbited yaws.
findings.fix_correction: Don't un-batch tall props into individual meshes. A bookshelf is about 28 parts, so 5 shelves would add about 140 meshes, or about 400 draw calls once shadow and outline passes are counted, which worsens the DR-24 overrun in finding 23. Instead, give tall-prop batches a per-instance opacity: an InstancedBufferAttribute read in an onBeforeCompile alpha, or alphaHash. Or swap a single prop out of its batch into a faded standalone clone only while the ray hits it. The multi-point ray (feet, chest, head) is a good addition.

findings.title: One trainee is painted job yellow (#ffc94d), the same hue as the plug and reel
findings.problem: The third trainee at (9,1.6) has color '#ffc94d', identical to the reel flanges, the plug coupler (#ffcc52) and the BLOBC 'yellow'. In the survey and the overstretch shot it reads as a yellow job object: a dropped reel or a lamp. That puts a blob-shaped coworker in the job-item colour, which breaks both DR-45 (no non-job thing in job yellow) and DR-52 (blob hues only on coworkers, and job yellow is reserved). The kit's BLOBC list itself contains #ffc94d, so any level can repeat this.
findings.fix: Change that trainee to '#b392f0' (lilac) or '#5b9cf0' in playground.ts:19. Remove '#ffc94d' from BLOBC in kit.ts:10, replacing it with a coral like '#f6a07a', so no blob defaults to job yellow.
findings.verify: Retake playground-models-02 and -49. No yellow blob; the only yellow in the room is job items.
findings.verify_reason: playground.ts:20 gives the third trainee '#ffc94d', and kit.ts:10 BLOBC contains '#ffc94d'. In my shots the trainee reads as a yellow blob in job-item yellow. It has eyes and headphones, so it still reads as a coworker. It conflicts with DR-45 and DR-52 colour reservation rather than confusing play.

findings.title: The spool's remaining length can't be read at the game camera; the reel has no stand and sinks into its base
findings.problem:
The spool was added so players can read the cable left (P4). But the anchor reel's axis runs along world z (cyl 'z'), and the default camera looks almost straight down −z (yaw 0.14). The player therefore sees the front flange disc face-on, and the white wound cable is hidden behind it except for a thin sliver above the rim. Start crop -56 and after-payout crop -55 differ only by that sliver, about 40 px of reel at default zoom.
The model is also unfinished:
- The flanges (r .336, centre y .35, so the bottom is at y .014) sink about 6.6 cm into the 0.06 m INK base plate (top at y .08).
- The drum and axle float with no A-frame or cradle holding them.
- There is no crank or cable guide where the lead leaves.
As the 'star' prop next to spawn, it reads as a yellow cotton reel on a tile.
evidence: src/game.ts:90-91 (anchor group at y .35; flanges cyl(.336,.336,.056,24,'z'); base box(.5,.06,.5) at y -.3)
findings.fix: Turn the anchor group 90° (group.rotation.y=Math.PI/2) so the drum's side faces the default camera and the winding thickness reads directly. Raise the axle to y .44 so the flanges clear the plate. Add two A-frame legs per side (box(.05,.5,.05) ±0.3 rad), joined at the axle hubs, on a rounded base rbox(.7,.05,.5,.03). Add a crank handle (cyl + knob) on one hub and a cable guide ring (Torus .06) where the lead exits. Optional: paint 3 bands on the drum (green, yellow, red) that the winding covers in turn, so 'nearly empty' reads as red.
findings.verify: Crop the reel at the default camera at start and after walking to (5.8,-5.5) (d.mjs). The visible winding thickness differs by at least 10 px at 1440×900. In a zoom-9 orbit, no flange intersects the base.
findings.verify_reason: In game.ts:90-91 the anchor group sits at y .35, the flanges are cyl r .336 along z (bottom at y .014), and the INK base box(.5,.06,.5) is at local y -.3 (world .02-.08). The flanges therefore sink about 6.6 cm into the plate, with no frame, crank or guide. The default yaw .14 looks along −z at the flange face. The reviewer's crops -56 and -55 show the winding only as a thin white sliver above the front flange, and the before/after difference is small.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-12-hold-plug-side.jpg (reel side view: no stand, flange on the plate)

findings.title: The 'graph' poster is hung over a window, and the window mullion passes in front of it
findings.problem: wallArt(back,'graph',8.4,1.9,.18) puts the poster's face (world z ≈ -9.795) in the middle of the window at x 8.2 (windowXs gives -7.8 … 8.2; the window spans x 7.0–9.4, y 1.23–2.68). The window's centre mullion and frame (front at z ≈ -9.76) stand proud of the poster face, so a vertical white bar runs through the poster. The poster appears pasted onto the glass. It sits behind the lamp and sits in the frame of the win push-in, the most-viewed shot of the level.
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:65 and src/levels/dressing.ts:27-31 (windowXs/windowUnit: mullion box .06 at z+.04)
findings.fix: Move the poster into the 0.8 m pier between the windows at x 5.0 and 8.2, at (6.6,1.75,.18), scale .8 (width .58 m). Or put it on the side wall at local x 4 (world z -4). Add a guard in backWindows() or wallArt that skips art whose x lies within a window's span, or a one-line unit test.
findings.verify: Retake the win push-in (d.mjs, playground-models-47). The poster sits on plain wallpaper with no frame bars crossing it.
findings.verify_reason: decor.ts:104 sets wallArt(back,'graph',8.4,1.9,.18). windowXs(20) gives windows at -7.8, -4.6, -1.4, 1.8, 5.0 and 8.2, so the poster lands on the x 8.2 window. The reviewer's crop -59 shows the window's vertical mullion running in front of the poster face, and my win push-in shows the poster pasted onto the glass.

findings.title: Every dynamic prop rests about 2.7 cm below the visible floor (the floor collider top is at y −0.025)
findings.problem: The floor collider is solid(this,w,.35,d,0,-.2,0), whose top is at y −0.025. The visible floor plane is drawn at y +0.002. Props settle on the collider, so every box, cone, bin, chair and beanbag sinks about 2.7 cm into the visible floor. The scene census shows boxes (h .6) centred at y .27, so their bottom is at −0.03, cone base plates at y 0.0 and beanbag base spheres reaching −0.036. Paper sheets (h .03) settle at y −0.01 to −0.02, so their top is only 3 mm above the floor or under it. That invites z-fighting and shimmer at distance, and some sheets vanish into the floor. Pip is offset by the controller and stands on the visible floor, so props look sunk next to Pip. The contact shadows land on the floor plane, not at the props' true base. Applies to every cable-floor level.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/playground-models/scene.json (box y .27, cone base y 0, paper y −0.01/−0.02, beanbag base y .18 with r .216)
findings.fix: Change game.ts:117 to solid(this,l.width,.35,l.depth,0,-.175,0) so the collider top is at y 0.0, and keep the visible floor at y .002. Check that Pip's spawn y (.91) and the controller offset (.025) still ground Pip. Give paper a minimum resting top of y ≥ .01 (paper h .03 → .02 and a mass of .05 is fine).
findings.verify: Re-run scene.mjs. Box instances rest at y ≈ .30 and paper at ≥ .01. A zoom-9 two-frame diff over the litter shows no flicker. Re-run tests/layout.spec.ts.
findings.verify_reason: game.ts:117 builds the floor collider as solid(...,.35,...,-.2), so its top is at y −0.025, while the floor plane is at y .002 (decor.ts:27). I measured instanced prop bottoms in the live scene: box bodies, cone bases, bins, plant pots and shelf posts all sit at y −0.025. All six pin centres rest at y .285 (half-height .31). The props sink 2.7 cm into the visible floor.
extra_evidence: v1.mjs instance-bottom probe: ExtrudeGeometry c98f5a (box) bottom −0.025; cone base −0.025; bin −0.025; plant pot −0.025
Pip rests at y 0.77 (capsule bottom 0.0), avatar drawn at p.y−.78 (game.ts:414)
findings.fix_correction: Raising the collider top to 0 also lifts Pip. Its capsule then rests at y .795 because of the controller offset of .025, and with game.ts:414 drawing the avatar at p.y−.78, Pip's boots would float about 1.5 cm above the floor (today they sit 1 cm into it). Change the avatar offset in game.ts:414 to p.y−.795, or derive it from the collider. Re-check the reel, socket and anchor heights, which are hard-coded to the visible floor.

findings.title: The cable is a 20 cm fire hose as thick as the plug, and pale when slack
findings.fix: Set the hose radius to .055 (game.ts:304) and the Pulses capsule radius to .055 (actors.ts:82). Give the coupler a strain-relief collar cyl(.07,.09,.08) where the lead enters, so the plug stays clearly bigger than the cord. Keep strain white per AGENTS 4, but darken the rest tone to '#e9e2d0' and add a thin ink 'tracer' stripe along the cable (a second vertex-colour band), so a slack cable reads on pale floors. That also helps once the floor value drops (DR-54).
findings.verify: Retake playground-models-41 and -44. Cable diameter is under 60% of the plug head's diameter, and at strain 0 the cable/floor luma difference is ≥ 25 in a crop.
findings.verify_reason: In code, game.ts:304 sets the hose radius to .1 (20 cm diameter), close to the coupler's r .11-.13 (prefabs.ts:102). My side view shows the hose about as thick as Pip's forearm and plug. The luma claim is weaker than stated: I measured slack cable 227 against floor 203 (24 luma), not 13. Whether 20 cm is 'too thick' is a style judgment: the cable is the hero object and must read at zoom 38.
findings.fix_correction: Don't jump straight to .055. At zoom 38 a 5.5 cm cable may drop under DR-59's 8 px minimum and lose its role as the room's main object (AGENTS: the cable is the star). Try .07–.075, check the width in px at zoom 38 and zoom 9, and keep the tracer-stripe idea for slack contrast.

findings.title: Sprint dust puffs are outlined toon spheres in floor colour, so they show as hollow ink rings
findings.problem: Footstep and sprint dust uses toon('#e6dfd2') on an icosahedron. That material keeps the OutlineEffect hull, and its fill matches the floor, so every puff renders as a little blue-ink circle on the floor (crop -54). They trail Pip along every walk (shots -23, -30, -42, -43, -53) and look like stray wire rings or decals. DR-56 says effects are never outlined.
findings.fix: In particles.ts:35, give dust a material with outlineParameters={visible:false}: a cached toon clone with userData.outlineParameters.visible=false, or a transparent MeshBasicMaterial that fades opacity like smoke (opacity .45·t). Tint it 10–15 luma darker than the floor so it reads as a scuff, not a void.
findings.verify: Run a 3 s sprint and take two zoom-9 shots. No ink-outlined circles on the floor. Retake playground-models-42.
findings.verify_reason: particles.ts:35 gives dust toon(color), a plain cached toon material without outlineParameters.visible=false, so OutlineEffect draws its hull. Smoke, sparks, stars and rings all opt out (particles.ts:14, 33). game.ts:328 spawns sprint dust in '#e6dfd2' at y .06, with the same fill tone as the floor. The reviewer's crop -54 shows the resulting floor-coloured disc with a blue ink outline ring.
extra_evidence: src/render/particles.ts:14,33 (the other effect materials disable outlines; dust does not)

findings.title: The win lamp's glow sprite is 3.6× its shade at opacity 0.6 and washes the win shot; the lamp model is crude
findings.problem:
lightUp() adds a 3 m additive glow sprite at opacity .6 on a 0.84 m shade, plus a point light (intensity 10, distance 9) and a lamp pool. In the win push-in (shots -46 to -48) the left half of the frame bleaches to cream: the bookshelf, boxes and Pip's top half lose their toon bands, which weakens the 'Pip together with the working machine' payoff. DR-66 caps glow at opacity ≤ .5 and ≤ 1.5× its source.
The lamp model itself has problems:
- The base is an INK disc of radius .42 that reads as a black hole or puddle at the game camera (shots -23, -25).
- The unlit bulb is a dark grey ball under the shade (the old 'black bowling ball' note).
- The 0.9 m arm passes through the top of the open shade.
- There is no junction box or cable entry.
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:89-91 (base cyl .34/.42 INK; arm box .9 at y 2.68; shade top r .18 at y 2.72; bulb #6b6f84)
findings.fix:
In lightUp(): glow size 1.2, opacity .45; pointLamp intensity 6, distance 7; lampPool opacity .22.
Model:
- Base: cyl(.22,.28,.12) in DMETAL with a rubber ring torus.
- Add a hood cap cyl(.2,.2,.05) closing the top of the shade.
- Mount the shade from a short drop rod below the arm, not through it.
- Unlit bulb: a frosted '#e9e4d6' toon sphere.
- Add a small junction box rbox(.14,.2,.1) at y .5 on the post, with the conduit from the socket and switch (see the switch finding).
findings.verify: Retake the win push-in (d.mjs -47). Pip's toon ramp is still visible, and the median luma of the left half is under 225. In a game-camera crop the lamp base reads as a base, not a hole.
findings.verify_reason: In code, decor.ts:93 adds glow(... ,3,.6), a pointLamp with intensity 10 and distance 9, and a lampPool. That breaks DR-66's limits (opacity ≤ .5, size ≤ 1.5× source). The washout is overstated, though. In my win push-in, Pip's toon bands are still visible and the left half's median luma is 201, which already passes the reviewer's own verify threshold (<225). The black base disc reads as a dark puddle or hole in my close-ups, as claimed.

findings.title: Copy-paste clutter: identical bookshelves, paired plant clones and a bin row along the wall; books are saturated candy bars
findings.problem:
The five bookshelves are identical in every respect. Each has 7 books per shelf, all the same size (0.14×0.34), and the colour order depends only on the shelf's y (books[(k+round(y*5))%6]), so the pattern repeats exactly (shots -19, -22, -24). At zoom 9 the books read as rounded candy bars or soap bars in fully saturated CHAIRC hues; DR-51 wants books desaturated. On the top shelf the books (top at y .97) stand higher than the 0.9 m posts.
The 14 plants are one model at one rotation. Eight of them come as four side-by-side 'plants' pairs, at (-6.36,-8.84)/(-6.48,-8.08), (-6.59,-6.35)/(-6.71,-5.59), (6.99,-3.3)/(6.23,-3.42) and (-8.84,6.79)/(-8.08,6.91), so the clones are obvious.
The fill pass lays a neat row of bins plus paper along the left wall at x≈-9, at z -0.3, 1.1, 2.47 and 5.48 (shots -01, -10).
evidence: src/props/prefabs.ts:123-125 (bookshelf: fixed book size, colour index from k and y only)
src/levels/clutter.ts:46 (plants pair), :69-73 (fill pass on a regular grid, jitter .45·st)
findings.fix:
Bookshelf:
- Pass `variant` from the shelf recipe (clutter.ts:44, variant:Math.floor(r()*8)).
- In prefabs.ts build books from a seeded rng: heights .24–.36, widths .08–.16, one leaning book and one gap per shelf, a bookend on some shelves.
- Desaturated palette: '#c46a6a', '#6f8fb8', '#7fa58a', '#d9b86a', '#9a88b8', '#86b5ae'.
- Make the posts h+.08 so they cap the top row.

Plant: build 3 variants (leaf cluster rotation, a spiky snake-plant variant, a round bush), add a pot rim torus and a dark soil disc, and pass a random variant from the recipe.

Fill pass:
- Increase jitter to .9·st.
- Skip 35% of fill cells at random.
- Cap 'bin' at 4 per room.
findings.verify: Re-run scene.mjs: no two bookshelves share a book colour sequence, and plant instances use at least 3 geometries. Retake survey -02: no evenly spaced row of identical props is visible.
findings.verify_reason:
Every claim checks out in code:
- prefabs.ts:125: books are a fixed .14×.34 and coloured by (k+round(y*5)); no variant is used, so all 5 shelves are identical.
- Books' top at y .97 is above the post tops at .9.
- plants (clutter.ts:46) is a fixed pair, and plant (prefabs.ts:84-86) has one model.
- The fill pass jitter is .45·st (clutter.ts:74).
The scene census found 14 plants and 13 bins. My start shot shows the evenly spaced bin row along the left wall and the repeated shelves.
extra_evidence: v3.mjs: plant pot batch count 14, bin 13, bookshelf posts 20 (=5 shelves)

findings.title: The room is thin and litter-heavy: 109 props, a third of them trash, no carts or cabinets, an empty centre-right
findings.problem: The playground has 109 props on 400 m², 0.27 per m². The DR-67 standard is about 0.39 per m² (250 props on a 32×20 floor). Roughly a third of the props are litter or trash: 17 paper sheets, 13 bins and 5 mugs. The level asks for 'cart' and 'cabinets' recipes, but the lanes and fixtures leave no room and none were placed (scene census). The x 2–8, z -4…3 quarter holds only cones, the yellow trainee and one shelf (survey -02, -42). It reads as an empty warehouse floor with trash around the edges rather than a dressed 'training bay', and the centre gives the slingshot little to fling.
evidence: mockups/review5/tools/playground-models/scene.json (paper ×17, bin ×13, mug ×5; no cart/cabinet geometry present)
src/levels/playground.ts:5 (recipes incl. cart, cabinets; max 90; lanes r 1.3)
findings.verify: snap().props ≥ 150. Every 4×4 m walkable cell has ≥ 3 props (heat map from scene.json). The routes.spec playground tests still pass with the same clutter seed.
findings.verify_reason: snapshot().props = 109 on a 20×20 room (0.27 per m²). DR-67's 250 props on 640 m² is about 0.39 per m², or about 156 for this room. My batch census found 17 paper, 13 bins and 14 plants, and no cart or cabinet geometry at all, even though playground.ts:5 lists both recipes.
extra_evidence: v3.mjs: cart tray batch none, cabinet body batch none, paper 17, bin 13

findings.title: Pallets overlap each other and are flat slabs; cage reels float; cooler and plant pots have too few cues
findings.problem:
Several small fixtures have overlaps or too little detail:
- The two pallets under the box stack, at (8.2,8.2) and (8.9,8.4), are each 1.1×0.9 m. They interpenetrate over a 0.4×0.7 m area with coplanar tops at y .14. g.audit can't see this, because it does not test fixed against fixed.
- The pallets are plain 0.14 m slabs with no slats or gaps, so they read as trays or cardboard sheets (shots -32, -33).
- The supply-cage reels hang at y .36 with flange radius .32, so their bottoms float 4 cm above the floor. At the game camera the red one reads as a red ball or apple behind bars (shots -13, -15).
- The cage has no roof rail, door or base frame.
- The water cooler is a rounded box plus a straight cylinder: no tap, no drip tray, no inverted-bottle neck (2 cues, shot -22).
- Plant pots have no rim or soil (shot -23).
findings.fix:
Pallets: place them side by side without overlap at (8.55,7.75) and (8.55,8.7), with the box props updated to match (playground.ts:15). Model each as 3 stringers box(1.1,.09,.1) and 5 top boards box(.2,.03,.9) with 4 cm gaps.
Cage:
- reels at y .32 on a small cradle box(.5,.06,.3);
- recolour (see the false-affordance finding);
- add a top frame and a door with a hasp (box .05×.1×.04).
Cooler: add a tap block with two spigots (red/blue cyl .02), a drip tray rbox(.3,.03,.18), a bottle neck cyl(.08,.2,.12) at the top, and a cup dispenser tube on the side.
Plant: add a pot rim torus(.26,.03) and a soil disc cyl(.23,.23,.02) '#6b4a2e'.
findings.verify: Zoom-9 shots of the stack, cage and cooler (c.mjs). Pallets show slats and gaps, no reel floats, and the cooler shows ≥ 4 cues. A fixed-vs-fixed overlap check (extend audit or a unit test over decor solids) reports none.
findings.verify_reason: The pallets are box(1.1,.14,.9) at (8.2,8.2) and (8.9,8.4) (decor.ts:95). Their x spans 7.65–8.75 and 8.35–9.45 and their z spans 7.75–8.65 and 7.95–8.85, so they overlap by 0.4×0.7 m with coplanar tops. They are plain slabs. The cage reels sit at y .36 with flange r .32, so their bottoms are 4 cm above the floor (decor.ts:112). The cooler is two parts (prefabs.ts:129). Plant pots have no rim or soil (prefabs.ts:85).

findings.title: At low or close orbits, the side wall's cutaway stub is a bare tan slab that hides Pip's legs
findings.problem: Orbiting so the camera sits behind the left wall, with Pip near the how-to board at (-8.4,-0.3), shows the 1.06 m lower wall as a featureless tan block filling the bottom 40% of the frame at zoom 9. It cuts Pip off at the knees (shot -16). The lower part never fades (only the upper part folds), and its outside face has no trim, baseboard or panel line. That makes it a large flat single-colour face, against DR-62, and an occluder that ignores DR-12.
evidence: src/levels/decor.ts:31-43 (shellWall: lower part box(length,1.06,thick) plain WALL_LOW; only 'upper' folds)
findings.fix: When a shell wall faces away from the camera, drop the lower part as well, to a 0.3 m lip (scale its y or swap to a short lip mesh). Or register the lower wall meshes as occluders that fade to 0.25 when the Pip ray hits them. Give the outside face a cap, a baseboard and two panel grooves so a visible exterior reads as a finished wall.
findings.verify: Repeat the b.mjs how-to-board visit with orbit 300 at zoom 9. Pip's boots are visible, and the wall shows trim or is reduced to a lip.
findings.verify_reason: shellWall (decor.ts:35) keeps the 1.06 m lower box opaque and never fades it; only `upper` folds (game.ts:385-386). The reviewer's shot -16 shows the tan stub filling the lower frame. I found a worse case. After plugging in, at zoom 9 and orbit −450 near the lamp, the camera goes behind the back wall, and the lower wall plus its cap fill about 75% of the frame and hide Pip completely. That happens right at the socket and lamp payoff.
extra_evidence: mockups/review5/shots/verify-playground-models-18-plugged-close-o-450.jpg (Pip fully hidden behind the back wall's lower stub)
findings.fix_correction: Raise this to P1. It fully hides Pip at a normal orbit near the job target (DR-12). Fading the lower part to ≤0.25 when the Pip ray hits it, or dropping it to a 0.3 m lip when the outside faces the camera, is the right fix. Use cloned materials (plain() is cached and shared).

findings.title: The objective marker is a flat unoutlined cone at a fixed 2.1 m: it pierces the lamp post and drops into Pip's hat
findings.problem:
The objective marker is a ConeGeometry(.22,.42) in a MeshBasicMaterial with no outline, shading or second tone. It is placed at y 2.1±0.18 whatever is below it:
- For 'Switch the lamp on' it sits exactly on the lamp post's axis, so the post runs through it (shot -45).
- For 'Pick up the plug' when the plug lies at Pip's feet, it sinks into the hard hat (crown at y about 1.76; shots -10, -62).
- For the socket step it overlaps the lamp shade at y 2.4 (shot -44).
Its pale #ffd84a reads weakly against the 205-luma cream floor and the yellow hat. DR-44 asks for an outlined, 2-tone marker that sits above clutter.
findings.fix: In objectives.ts, set the marker y to max(2.1, the target's highest nearby geometry + 0.5): for example a raycast down from y 4 at the target, or a per-step `height`. Use 3.2 for the lamp switch step, or point at the new switch box instead of the post. When Pip is within 1 m of the target, use Pip head + 0.7. Give it an INK back-face outline (a slightly larger cone with side:BackSide) and a two-tone fill (darker lower half), and keep the bob.
findings.verify: Retake -44, -45 and -62. The marker never intersects geometry, and it has a dark rim at least 2 px wide at 1440×900.
findings.verify_reason: objectives.ts:97-98 builds a MeshBasic cone with its outline disabled. objectives.ts:118 places it at a fixed y 2.1±.18, so it intersects the lamp post for the switch step (my shot) and sinks into Pip's hat when the plug lies at Pip's feet (reviewer shot -62). One correction: the colour is multiplied by 1.5 (objectives.ts:97), so it reads bright rather than 'pale'. The breach of DR-44 is the missing outline and two-tone shading.

findings.title: Pip's hard-hat ridge ends stick out of the flattened dome as two 'cat ears' (F9 still open)
findings.problem: The helmet is a flattened sphere (scale z .17) with a straight 0.48 m ridge box laid on top at z 1.72. The dome curves away beneath the ridge's ends, so the front and back ends stand up as two bumps. From behind or three-quarter views they read as cat ears (crops -57, -60). Pip is in every shot of the tutorial, so this is the first silhouette a player learns.
evidence: tools/create_assets.py:61-63 (Helmet sphere scale .17; HelmetRidge cube (.035,.24,.035) at z 1.72)
findings.fix: In tools/create_assets.py, replace the HelmetRidge cube with a curved ridge that follows the dome: a torus segment (major radius ≈ dome radius .30, minor .03, arc 100°) rotated to run front to back. Alternatively shorten the cube to .30 long and sink it .02 into the dome with a bevel of .03. Re-export the glTF.
findings.verify: Pip crops from front, back and side at zoom 9 (b.mjs reel-back and orbit shots). The helmet outline is one smooth dome with a low central ridge and no bumps at either end.
findings.verify_reason: In tools/create_assets.py, the Helmet is an ellipsoid at z 1.59 with semi-axes (.32,.29,.17) and HelmetRidge is a cube of half-size (.035,.24,.035) at z 1.72. At y=±.24 the dome surface is at z ≈ 1.59+.17·√(1−(.24/.29)²) ≈ 1.685, while the ridge top is at 1.755, so both ends stand about 7 cm proud. My three-quarter shots show the two bumps as cat ears.

findings.title: 778 draw calls at the start view and 782 in the survey, three times the 250 budget
findings.problem: snapshot().drawCalls reports 778 at the default start camera and 782 in the survey (fps 60 on this host GPU). The scene has only 340 meshes (all MeshToon or MeshBasic), so the count is roughly tripled by the shadow pass plus the OutlineEffect re-render, and the 79 InstancedMesh batches are each drawn three times. DR-24 sets about 250 so dense rooms hold up on weaker GPUs. The playground is the lightest room and already exceeds it.
evidence: a.mjs output: start dc 778, survey dc 782, props 109
scene.mjs output: meshes 340, 79 instanced batches, 5 lights (hemi, ambient, 3 directional)
findings.fix: Merge each prop kind's parts into one geometry with vertex colours before instancing (like blobMesh in kit.ts:75-82), so a box is 1 batch rather than 6 and the room needs about 15 batches. Exclude tiny parts (box labels, ink lines) from castShadow. Restrict OutlineEffect to a layer that skips decals and paper.
findings.verify: snap().drawCalls ≤ 250 at start and in the survey. fps unchanged. Visual diff of playground-models-01 unchanged.
findings.verify_reason: I measured snap().drawCalls = 780 at the start camera, with 109 props and 79 instanced batches, against DR-24's limit of about 250.

findings.title: The cable passes through dynamic props instead of draping over them
findings.problem: The rope only wraps level.obstacles (the two pillars). Boxes, bookshelves and chairs are ignored by the rope path, so a dragged cable runs straight through a cardboard box (shot -61) and through tipped shelves. Combined with the hose's 20 cm thickness, this is very visible at the close camera, and it undercuts 'the cable is physical'.
evidence: src/game.ts:271-279 (rope route built from this.obstacles only)
findings.fix: In drawCable(), after cablePath, lift hose points that fall inside a prop's AABB to that prop's top + hose radius + .02 (a drape). Take the AABB from prop.body.translation() and the prefab size; the cost is about 110 props × about 40 points per frame, which is cheap. Optionally, push light props (mass < 3) sideways when the taut cable sweeps through them, which also feeds the slingshot.
findings.verify: Drag the plug past the crate row at z 4.6 (routes.spec slingshot path) and take a zoom-9 shot. The cable rides over the boxes, and no hose section is hidden inside a box.
findings.verify_reason: Partly wrong as written. simulateCable (game.ts:273-280) does wrap furniture: every prop of mass ≥3 within 1.2 m of the rope (chairs, bookshelves, beanbags) is added as an obstacle. So the statement that the rope only wraps the two pillars and ignores bookshelves and chairs is incorrect. Light props (box mass 2, bin, cone, plant, paper) are excluded, and the cable does pass through cardboard boxes. My practice-wall shot shows the hose running through a box.
findings.fix_correction: Scope the fix to light props (mass < 3), since heavier furniture is already wrapped. Either include boxes as wrap obstacles: lower the threshold to mass ≥2, or include them when they are not being dragged. Or keep the vertical drape lift for props below 3 kg only. The strain>.88 drag at game.ts:333 already pulls props of mass ≤15 along the rope, so a drape must not fight that.

notes.fun: The core toy works and feels good. The cable's strain ramp (white, then yellow, orange and a thick red) reads beautifully at the game camera (shots -43, -49, -50). The slingshot prompt appears at the limit, and the lamp payoff (glow, pool, confetti, Pip cheering) lands. The clean solve took 10.2 s and earns A/A/A. Two things undercut the fun in model and art terms. First, the six 'pins' are recoloured traffic cones that Pip bowls over just by walking, so the strike bonus and confetti fire without the cable (shot -33). The slingshot's designed reward is free, and the pins don't look like pins. Second, the slingshot run itself flung nothing visible in my scripted overstretch (fastestProp 0 after 1.5 s, shots -51/-52), and the centre of the room is thin, so a fling has little to hit. Pushing a 24 kg bookshelf over by walking (shots -22, -23, -61) is a nice accidental slapstick moment. Coworkers, though, have no colliders, so the most obvious comedy target (bonking a trainee) can't happen.
notes.playability:
Controls and the route are fine: walkTo reached every fixture, and the clean route needed no detour. The camera is the main problem:
- Bookshelves (1.8 m) and the supply cage never fade and hide Pip (shots -17, -21).
- When a pillar does fade, it leaves its cap and plinth floating (shots -18, -20).
- The side-wall stub fills the frame at low orbits (shot -16).
The plug starts under Pip's feet, so the first frame shows no job item. Pip walks through coworkers. 778 draw calls is three times the budget even in this light room. g.audit(.02) at start reports only 3 overlaps, all paper sheets 3 cm inside beanbags. It cannot see fixed-vs-fixed overlaps such as the two pallets at (8.2,8.2) and (8.9,8.4), decor-only interpenetrations (poster vs window mullion, target ring vs lamp base, double socket), or the coworkers. g.close() returned [] for every script: no console or page errors.
notes.teaching:
The wordless how-to board on the side wall (reel → cable → plug → socket → lamp) is excellent and exactly the 'play by doing' language the room needs (shot -14). Three model problems weaken it:
- The socket on the poster is a recognisable socket, but the real target is a blank dark box. It has no face or slots, its geometry is duplicated, and the plug's pins come out of its back.
- There is no switch model at all: 'Switch the lamp on' means pressing E at the bare post base, so the room never shows that a switch closes the loop.
- The practice wall's five sockets, one glowing green, accept nothing and give no feedback, which teaches the opposite of 'a plug that looks in snaps in'.
Adding a visible switch box with a toggle and pilot light, a proper socket face with a pilot LED, and a conduit linking socket → switch → bulb would make the loop visible without text. Making the practice wall a working warm-up (an LED lights) would teach plugging before the real job.
